questions.question: What is the quantile function associated with a distribution function $F$?
options: $Q(u)=F(u)+1$ for all real $u$
$Q(u)=\inf\{x\in\mathbb{R}\colon F(x)\ge u\}$ for $0<u<1$
$Q(u)=P(X=u)$ for every $u$
$Q(u)=E[X\mid X=u]$

questions.question: What range of $u$ is used for the quantile function?
options: $u\le0$
$u\ge1$
All real numbers without restriction

questions.question: What is another name for the quantile function?
options: Probability mass function
Standard deviation
Inverse CDF
Sample mean

questions.question: What does a quantile function tell you?
options: The cumulative probability up to a chosen value $x$.
The probability mass or density at a chosen value.
The value at a chosen cumulative probability level.
The average value below a chosen probability level.

questions.question: What kind of inverse is the quantile function?
options: A reciprocal of the variance of $X$
A complement of an event
A derivative of a density
A generalized inverse of the CDF

questions.question: What is the median in quantile language?
options: The quantile at probability level zero
The quantile at probability one half
The maximum possible value
The variance at the mean

questions.question: What does the ninety-fifth percentile of delivery time represent?
options: The variance of delivery time
The probability of zero delivery time
A quantile of the delivery-time distribution
The sample size of the delivery-time observations

questions.question: What role does a quantile function play in simulation?
options: It turns target samples into uniform numbers for any distribution.
It turns uniform numbers into probabilities of the target outcomes.
It turns uniform numbers into target samples only for continuous $F$.
It turns uniform numbers into samples of a target distribution.

questions.question: Which input is appropriate for $Q(u)$?
options: $u=\operatorname{Var}(X)$ with no probability scale

questions.question: Why does the definition use an infimum?
options: It forces all the distributions to be uniform
It computes a variance directly
It handles CDFs that are flat or have jumps
It makes the quantile always negative

questions.question: How are quantiles related to percentiles?
options: Percentiles are CDF values given as percentages.
The $95$th percentile equals $Q(95)$ rather than $Q(0.95)$.
Percentiles are quantiles at percentage levels.
Percentiles apply to samples, quantiles to distributions.

questions.question: Why is the quantile function useful for describing distribution positions?
options: It identifies values by cumulative level.
It identifies values by their density height.
It identifies values by distance from the mean.
It gives the cumulative probability of each value.

questions.question: For a distribution with median $m$, what quantile statement is natural?
options: $F(0.5)=m$ for a unique median.
$Q(m)=0.5$ for a unique median.
$Q(0.25)=m$ for a unique median.
$Q(0.5)=m$ for a unique median.

questions.question: To generate exponential samples from uniforms, what function is applied?
options: The exponential distribution function
The exponential quantile function
The exponential density function
The exponential survival function

questions.question: Why is a quantile function not necessarily an ordinary inverse function?
options: CDFs have flats/jumps, needing a generalized inverse.
CDFs are strictly decreasing, so the inverse flips the order.
Quantiles invert the density, not the CDF itself.
Ordinary inverses exist only for linear functions like $F(x)=x$.

questions.question: The quantile function inverts the CDF $F$. Which interpretation does $Q(0.95)$ have?
options: A value at the cumulative probability level $0.95$
The probability that $X$ is at most $0.95$
A value exceeded with probability $0.95$
The average of the largest five percent of values

questions.question: If a CDF jumps from $0.4$ to $0.7$ at $x=2$, what value should $Q(0.5)$ select under the infimum definition?
Let $Q$ be a quantile function whose argument is a probability level $u\in(0,1)$. Why is the proposed evaluation $Q(1.2)$ invalid?
options: The argument of $Q$ must be a value in the support of $X$
Quantile levels must be whole percentages from $0$ to $100$
The quantile level must lie between $0$ and $1$
$Q$ is defined only where the CDF is strictly increasing
